content:
Sam: Heads-up — planning a gradual canary for release v3.8.2 starting today at 18:00 UTC. Primary goal: rollout model-serving runtime improvements with minimal user impact.

Sam: Plan outline: 0->1% (15m), 1->5% (30m), 5->25% (45m), 25->100% (staged over 2h). Cohorts: mobile-first (iOS/Android) then web; geo order: US -> EU -> APAC.

Jess: Who's on deploy? I can own the 1->5% wedge and watch metrics for the first hour.

Sam: @Jess — pls. Oliver will handle the 5->25% and the final ramp. I'll coordinate rollback paths and console updates.

Oliver: Got it. I'll be online from 17:30 UTC. Any special smoke checks beyond standard latencies?

Sam: Smoke checklist (short):
- p50/p95 latency by route (text-gen, chat) < baseline + 20%
- error rate (4xx/5xx) < 0.5% absolute increase
- token-per-second throughput within expected range
- KV-cache hit rate not decreased by >5%

Sam: Quick command for the smoke-run we use:
```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1b","prompt":"smoke test lorem"}' \
```

Maya: Should we pin a fallback model variant on the route in case of perf regression? E.g., rwd-1b-fp16 as auto-fallback.

Sam: Yes — we'll configure fallback to rwd-1b-compat (lower memory profile). Policy: auto-fallback at 2x baseline latency or >1% absolute error increase for 5m. Manual rollback if regression persists after fallback.

Jess: How are we selecting the initial 1% cohort? Random sample weighted by sessions, but exclude enterprise customers (they're on dedicated). Also exclude internal orgs and canary-testers.

Oliver: For rollout windows do we want time-of-day guards per region? EU lunchtime could be risky. I'm proposing EU ramp at 02:00-06:00 UTC to avoid peak.

Sam: Agreed. Schedule:
- US ramp starting 18:00 UTC
- EU ramp delayed to 02:00 UTC local window
- APAC roll after EU stable (+4h buffer)

deploy-bot: [deploy queued] v3.8.2 canary job scheduled by Sam at 2026-03-17T18:00:00Z :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Maya: Metrics dashboards — I pushed a temporary dashboard to the Console under "releases/v3.8.2-canary" with p50/p95, errors, kv-hit, and model-fallback counts. Link in the release notes.

Sam: Perfect. Communication plan: post canary start in #releases + ping on-call. If we hit thresholds, OLiver will attempt fallback config, Jess will run targeted smoke script for affected route, and I'll coordinate rollback.

Jess: If we need to rollback, what's the exact command?

Sam: Manual rollback (if automatic fallback insufficient):
```bash
# rollback to previous stable route version
redwood routes rollback --route text-gen --to-version v3.7.9 --force --reason "canary rollback"
```

Oliver: I'll monitor logs and tail the error rates. If anything looks off I'll shout in thread and escalate to eng-sre.

Maya: Also verifying alert thresholds: creating short-lived alerts for +0.5% error and +35% p95. They'll auto-resolve after 30m of stability.

Sam: Final ask: everyone confirm availability for their wedge and set status in the calendar block. If you can't make it, call it out now so we can reassign.

Jess: Confirmed 17:30-20:30 UTC.

Oliver: Confirmed 17:30-22:00 UTC.

Maya: I'll be on for the EU window and monitoring dashboards.

Sam: Thanks — starting the queue. I'll post updates in-thread and in #releases when each ramp completes. :rocket:
